article.title: Aspecto y cortesía
article.chapter: Selección aspectual avanzada — Выбор вида: продвинутый уровень

claims.summary: Discusses the use of imperfective and perfective aspects in Russian imperatives and their contribution to the pragmatic tone of the statement.
Explains how certain verbs with imperfective imperatives indicate an action that is already open or expected, while perfective imperatives focus on a concrete action expected to be completed.
Emphasizes that the level of courtesy depends on the entire construction and situation, not just the aspect of the verb.

links.notes: The Wikipedia page on Aspect (grammar) provides a comprehensive explanation of imperfective and perfective aspects in Russian, including their use in imperatives and their impact on the tone of the statement. The information directly supports the claim made in the article.

The Wikipedia page provides examples of imperfective and perfective imperatives, such as 'садитесь' (siéntese) and 'откройте окно' (Abra la ventana), illustrating how the aspect of the verb affects the perceived completion of the action. This directly supports the claim made in the article.

The Wikipedia page notes that the politeness of an imperative depends on the whole construction and situation, not just the aspect of the verb. This supports the claim made in the article that the value of courtesy depends on the construction and situation.
